headline: Apple launches 'Upgrade' leasing program for iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Apple Watch
summary: Apple's new 'Upgrade' program allows consumers to lease iPhones, Macs, iPads, and Apple Watches with monthly payments. It replaces the existing iPhone Upgrade Program and offers options to swap for new hardware, keep, or return devices at the end of the term.
details: Apple has officially launched its new 'Upgrade' program in the US, allowing consumers to lease iPhones, iPads, Apple Watches, and Macs. This program replaces the long-running iPhone Upgrade Program and standard financing options, with existing iPhone Upgrade Program users grandfathered in.

Monthly prices start at $17.99 for iPhone, $11.99 for Apple Watch and iPad, and $24.99 for Mac. Lease terms are 24 months for iPhones and Apple Watches, and 36 months for iPads and Macs, with an option to pay off early for an extra fee.

At the end of the lease, customers can upgrade to a newer device, purchase their current device with a one-time payment, or return it. The program is run by Klarna, requiring approval, and allows for AppleCare to be added to leased devices.

Not all devices are available; models like iPhone 16, MacBook Neo, and Studio Display are excluded. This launch follows recent price increases for many iPad and Mac models, with future iPhones also expected to be more expensive.

headline_marked: Perplexity's Personal Computer now on Windows, [[turning PCs into AI agents]]
headline: Perplexity's Personal Computer now on Windows, turning PCs into AI agents
summary: Perplexity's agentic tool, which acts as a general-purpose digital worker, is now available for Windows. It integrates with local files, Microsoft 365, and the web, rolling out to Max and Enterprise Max users from $200/month.
details: Perplexity has expanded its agentic Personal Computer tool to Windows, allowing computers running the world’s most popular OS to be used as a locally run AI system. Like the Mac version launched in April, it operates as a "general-purpose digital worker" that can access local files and apps to perform actions.

This launch builds on Personal Computer integrations with Microsoft’s 365 workspace apps and Teams virtual meeting software from May. The Windows version aims to bridge the remaining gap by operating directly inside the Windows environment, addressing enterprise work typically done locally.

Now Microsoft users can ask Computer to work across their local files, Microsoft Office 365, and the web in one place. Perplexity states it's built for the often messy way enterprise work gets done on local machines.
Personal Computer for Windows is rolling out to paying Max and Enterprise Max users today. These subscription tiers start from $200 per month.
Perplexity says the tool doesn’t train on company data. Personal Computer for Windows always notifies users before performing sensitive actions like sending emails and deleting files.
